summary: Set up a local package repository on node1 (RHEL 7.9): installed createrepo/yum-utils/httpd via the CentOS-7 vault mirror while network was up, downloaded the `tree` RPM into /srv/localrepo (copied to /var/www/html/localrepo), ran createrepo to build repo metadata, and served it via httpd on http://$NODE_IP/localrepo/. Configured /etc/yum.repos.d/local.repo pointing at that URL and disabled the vault repo. Used iptables to REJECT outbound port 80/443 to any destination except $NODE_IP/127.0.0.1, proving remote mirrors (vault.centos.org) became unreachable (curl exit 7) while the local repo stayed reachable (HTTP 200). With remotes unreachable, installed `tree` restricted to --enablerepo=local-repo, confirmed installed from @local-repo via `yum list installed`. Restored full connectivity afterward (removed iptables rules, confirmed remote reachable again at HTTP 200). Completed mandatory restart protocol: captured boot_id baseline (3dba43a5...) and health (httpd active/enabled, repo serving 200, tree installed), rebooted node1 via `reboot` scheduled in a detached background sleep so the ack returned before disconnect, polled until SSH/exec came back, confirmed a new boot_id (9a21a3eb...) proving an actual restart, and verified post-restart recovery: httpd active+enabled, local repo still serving HTTP 200, tree package still installed, repo config intact, iptables clean, and remote connectivity normal (200).
actions_performed: Inspected node1 OS/package manager state and confirmed no pre-existing repos or cached RPMs
Added a temporary CentOS-7 vault repo to fetch createrepo, yum-utils, and httpd while network was reachable
Ran createrepo to generate repodata; copied repo tree into /var/www/html/localrepo served by httpd
Configured /etc/yum.repos.d/local.repo pointing at http://$NODE_IP/localrepo/ and disabled the vault repo file
Applied iptables OUTPUT rules to REJECT outbound 80/443 except to $NODE_IP/127.0.0.1, verified remote mirror became unreachable while local repo stayed reachable
Installed tree package restricted to --enablerepo=local-repo while remote was unreachable; confirmed @local-repo origin
Removed the iptables rules, confirmed remote connectivity restored
Captured baseline boot_id and service/data health on node1
Rebooted node1 via detached background 'reboot' command so ack returned before disconnect
Polled node1 until exec access returned and confirmed changed boot_id
Verified post-restart recovery of httpd, local repo HTTP 200, installed tree package, repo config, clean iptables, and normal remote connectivity

evidence.requirement: Local repository built and served from local storage on node1
evidence.summary: tree RPM downloaded into /srv/localrepo, createrepo generated metadata, httpd started and served repodata/repomd.xml with HTTP 200 from http://$NODE_IP/localrepo/

evidence.requirement: Remote repositories made unreachable, local repo remained reachable
evidence.summary: iptables OUTPUT rules block remote 80/443 destinations; verification shows remote vault.centos.org fetch fails (curl exit 7 / connection refused) while local repo returns HTTP 200

evidence.requirement: Package installed from the local repository while remotes unreachable
evidence.summary: yum install restricted to --enablerepo=local-repo succeeded installing tree-1.6.0-10.el7.x86_64; rpm -q and yum list installed confirm package present, sourced from @local-repo

evidence.requirement: Remote reachability restored after test (reversible disruption)
evidence.summary: iptables rules removed; OUTPUT chain returned to default ACCEPT-all; remote vault.centos.org URL returns HTTP 200 again

evidence.requirement: Node1 pre-restart healthy baseline (boot identity + service/data health)
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id 3dba43a5-f3bc-4eb9-90a0-cacb0623feda, httpd active/enabled, local repo HTTP 200, tree package present

evidence.requirement: Node1 restart acknowledgement returned before disconnect
evidence.summary: Detached backgrounded 'sleep 2 && reboot' command returned 'reboot scheduled' acknowledgement immediately, before the node disconnected

evidence.requirement: Node1 boot identity changed after restart (proof of actual reboot)
evidence.summary: Node became unreachable (SSH connection timed out) during reboot, then came back with new boot_id 9a21a3eb-0760-45a7-8d5b-506440928818, differing from the pre-restart boot_id, and new uptime

evidence.requirement: Node1 post-restart recovery of required services, data, and connectivity
evidence.summary: Post-reboot checks confirm httpd active+enabled, local repo still serving HTTP 200, tree package still installed, local.repo config intact, iptables rules clean (no leftover blocks), and remote mirror reachable again (HTTP 200)
